scope: Explicit open-boundary operators in the native coupled P1 laminar research solver; product maturity remains incomplete

environment.compiler:
Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2)
Target: arm64-apple-darwin27.0.0
Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/usr/bin
environment.versions: First six exploratory controls precede added finite-viscosity guard, explicit body-force JSON and applied-traction correction for noslip error reporting. Their exact earlier core source was reconstructed and hash verified against execution records; that first executable was not retained. Regular refinements use the retained before-warped-fixture source/binary. Warped and sensitivity cases use final source/binary; adding the mesh writer does not change operator formulas.

method.traction: sigma n=t_D, using manufactured exact full stress for reference controls and zero traction for cylinder
method.normal-stress: sigma n=-p_D n, with no tangential applied stress; a different physical boundary problem, not a discretization failure
method.pseudo-traction: (nu G-pI)n=-p_D n; implicit -nu G^T n face-test contribution in full-symmetric-stress matrix; prescribed -p_D n on RHS
method.restriction: Pseudo-traction is one weak vector condition, not independent strong enforcement of both p=p_D and d_n u=0. It agrees with fully developed parallel analytic flows but does not prove equivalence with the old collocated product stencil.
method.implementation: Shared native stress/RT1 load/convection, unchanged B/-B^T. Only retained face-test rows are modified; internal static condensation remains exact without refactorization. Boundary load, implicit gradient work, bulk viscous/stabilization energy and volume force work are reported separately. Applied face traction entries are integrated P1 moments, not point stresses.
method.data: Right axis-aligned outlet. Other boundaries carry manufactured velocity; cylinder keeps its original horizontal symmetry. No general named-boundary product API added. Pressure on open manufactured problems is compared absolutely without mean removal.

physicalControls.normalization: U=L=1, pressure scale U^2; no universal physical acceptance threshold introduced
physicalControls.poiseuille: u=(4y(1-y),0), p=-8x, f=(8nu-8,0). At nu=1 Stokes f=0; nu=.1 NS controls explicitly include f=(-7.2,0) and are manufactured-flow checks, not an unforced channel benchmark.
physicalControls.warpedGeometry: Same unit-square boundary; X=x+.09 sin(2pi x)sin(2pi y), Y=y+.06 sin(pi x)sin(2pi y), interior nodes only, boundary nodes exact. Shared canonical nodes; native fromPolygons/makeFvMesh2D and topology write/read. This is a smooth nonorthogonal quadrilateral fixture, not a Cartesian cut-cell cylinder.

interpretation: All boundary choices can converge while representing different physical problems. Normal stress only is a deliberate different-boundary control, not a numerically failed solve.

Regular-grid P2 potential velocity and static pressure reproduce the parallel manufactured flow to algebraic precision. RT1 transported velocity retains spatial error; no quadratic exactness claim for all velocity representations.

Warped-grid P2 potential velocity tends to order 3, static pressure to order 2, RT1 transported velocity to order 2. These three nested smooth-grid levels do not establish general cut-cell or curved-wall accuracy.

Stopping controls remain linear 1e-13 relative and nonlinear 1e-9 residual/change in normalized reference units. One final warped case tightened to 1e-14 and 1e-11; actual field differences are recorded separately from spatial errors.
Only native research code and its driver changed. Old default closed/open state vectors reproduced byte-for-byte. No production defaults, quality gates or boundary settings migrated.
Original Re20 anomaly, original pressure-outlet equivalence, backflow stability, curved pressure qualification, large NS resource costs and product/App/platform integration remain open.
